meaning: Requirement code, DR-01 to DR-19.
Which vendors the requirement covers: by GST status, constitution (company, LLP, partnership, proprietorship), purchase category code, or an MSME declaration.
The document the vendor must send, for example GST registration certificate (Form GST REG-06) or ISO 45001 certificate.
Yes if the document must be received; No for optional papers such as a company profile, which are not verified.
Which versions of the document are accepted in its place, for example a cancelled cheque or a signed and stamped bank letter; blank when only one form exists.
What makes the document acceptable on its own, for example the GSTIN structure, the PAN fourth character, or not lapsed on the verification date.
Values on this document that must agree with the other documents, for example legal name, PAN or account holder; blank when nothing is compared.
Rule code. PRS = presence, LEG = legibility, VAL = validity, EXP = expiry, XDC = cross-document, DUP = master check, CHS = chase cadence, HND = handover.
The group the rule belongs to, in words: Presence, Legibility, Validity, Expiry, Cross-document, Master check, Chase cadence or Handover.
The rule itself in one or two sentences, as the desk applies it.
Which requests or documents the rule covers, for example every vendor, GST-registered vendors, or msme_declared = Y.
Which documents or tables the rule reads to decide, for example the GST certificate and the PAN document, or Vendor_Master_Extract.
What the desk does when the rule fails, usually a chase for a named document or a stop for human review; blank for chase cadence and handover rows.
Onboarding request number, VOR-26- followed by four digits; quoted in the subject of every email about the request.
Date the buyer raised the request. Formats vary (25-09-2026, 25.09.2026, 30/09/2026, 2026-09-29, 30 Sep 2026, Oct 1, 2026, 22-09-26); numeric dates that do not start with the year put the day first.
Name of the buyer at Ashvaka who wants this vendor.
The buyer's email address at ashvakagroup.in.
SAP code of the group company that will buy: AI10 Ashvaka Infrastructure, AC20 Ashvaka Cement and Building Materials, AE30 Ashvaka Energy, AL40 Ashvaka Logistics and Warehousing.
SAP plant code of the site, for example 1002 = Sanand Industrial Park Project, 2002 = Rajkot RMC Plant, 4001 = Bhiwandi Distribution Centre (full list in 00_INDEX).
Purchase category code, such as EQUIP_RENTAL, CIVIL_WORKS, MANPOWER, SECURITY or TRANSPORT; it decides which extra documents the vendor must send.
The buyer's free-text reason, for example Crane and DG set hire for Rajkot RMC Plant.
The vendor's name as the buyer typed it. It can be informal, with an M/s prefix or a short suffix, so it is not the legal name.
Person at the vendor the buyer gave as the contact; chases go to this person.
The contact's email address; capitalisation varies.
The contact's mobile number, written +91 followed by ten digits.
Legal form the vendor declared: private or public limited company, LLP, partnership or proprietorship, written several ways (Pvt Ltd Company, Private Ltd, Sole Proprietor, Partnership Firm).
State the vendor says it supplies from, written in full, for example Gujarat or Maharashtra.
City the vendor declared, for example Anand or Bhiwandi.
Y if the vendor says it is a registered MSME (it must then send a Udyam certificate), N if not.
Y if the vendor says it is registered under GST; N means a signed non-registration declaration replaces the GST certificate.
Buyer's estimate of yearly spend with the vendor in rupees. Formats vary: 66,00,000.00, ₹ 66,00,000.00, INR 66,00,000.00, Rs. 66,00,000/-, plain digits, and western comma grouping.
Reference on the supplier registration portal, SR- followed by seven digits.
Desk status: Documents awaited (nothing received yet) or Documents received.
Row number of the log, CL- followed by five digits.
The onboarding request the email belongs to.
What was sent: Document checklist sent (the first email listing every document), Chase 1 or Chase 2.
0 = document checklist, 1 = first chase, 2 = second chase.
When the email went out. Mostly 2026-09-07 10:17:00 in IST; some rows use 28-09-2026 17:13, and some are UTC with a Z or carry a +05:30 offset.
Desk staff member who sent it.
Vendor address the email went to.
Address copied, normally the buyer who raised the request.
The full text of the email, listing each document asked for or each problem found.
Mailbox thread reference, B1-T followed by four digits, shared by every message about the request.
Email Message-ID of this outgoing mail; vendor replies quote it in their In-Reply-To header.
The onboarding request the attachment was filed against.
When the email carrying the file arrived, IST, as 2026-09-07 17:41:00.
Address the email came from: usually the vendor contact, sometimes another vendor address, a personal mailbox, or a buyer forwarding the papers.
Path of the .eml file in mailbox/inbox/ that carried the attachment.
File name as the vendor sent it, for example pan copy.pdf or IMG_20260909_169381.pdf; the name does not reliably say what the file is.
Where the file is saved under documents/<request_id>/, renamed with a number only when a name repeats.
Number of pages, 1 to 4; a file with several pages can hold more than one document.
File size in kilobytes.
SAP vendor number, six digits, for example 200100.
Vendor name as stored on the master, first 35 characters; capitalisation and suffix style vary.
Rest of the name when it runs past 35 characters, for example Ltd; usually blank.
Short search key, the first ten letters of the name in capitals without spaces.
Street address.
City.
Two-letter state code, for example GJ = Gujarat, MH = Maharashtra, RJ = Rajasthan (not the two-digit GST state code).
Six-digit postal PIN code.
Country code, IN for India.
Phone number, +91 followed by ten digits.
Vendor email address on file.
Vendor PAN, ten characters; blank on some older records.
Vendor GSTIN, fifteen characters; blank on some older records.
Country of the bank account, IN.
IFSC of the vendor's bank branch, eleven characters.
Bank account number the vendor is paid into.
Name of the bank account holder.
Y if the vendor is recorded as an MSME, N if not.
Udyam registration number, in the form UDYAM-GJ-09-4740105; blank for non-MSME vendors.
SAP account group: ZDOM = domestic vendor, ZMSE = domestic MSME vendor.
Main purchase category the vendor supplies, using the same codes as the onboarding requests.
Date the vendor was created on the master, dd.mm.yyyy, between 2014 and 2025.
X = blocked for posting (payments and invoices stopped); blank = active.
X = marked for deletion; blank otherwise.
Group company codes the vendor is already set up for, separated by semicolons, for example AE30;AI10.
